Header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood Solutions); Laura Kim (Zenith Head of ML), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Evelyn Moore (Finance), Tom Briggs (Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya our SE, and Miguel. want to kick off with quick intros and what you're trying to accomplish today.
[00:12] Laura Kim: thanks Alex, Laura here. we're evaluating options to run a chat/assist vector search stack for our trader desk workflows - very latency sensitive, bursty during market opens. main question is cost per unit and how batching/caching might help.
[00:26] Samir Patel: yep, we have a 1st party data set, we want model outputs not to persist in a vendor-managed store; also curious about dedicated vs hosted, and what reserved capacity pricing looks like.
[00:40] Evelyn Moore: hi all, finance - our constraint is a $15k monthly production budget for the initial pilot. want clear numbers so we can model spend.
[00:50] Priya Rao: great, thanks. quick overview - Redwood hosted gives simple per-token billing and quick start; dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit costs at commit; private gives VPC/on-prem with self-managed infra. for cost levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, and routing policies.
[01:10] Tom Briggs: security quick note - we need SOC2, SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS for key material, and audit logs with 90 day retention. how do you handle that on hosted?
[01:22] Alex Chen: on hosted we offer SOC2, and we can integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest; for stricter folks we recommend Dedicated or Private where the control plane is customer-controlled. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[01:34] Laura Kim: can you walk through example numbers? say 1M tokens a day, mix of short and long chats, target p95 latency under 350ms.
[01:45] Priya Rao: sure - rough ballpark: hosted per-token is X (placeholder), but with batching and prefix cache you can drop effective per-token cost by 20-50% depending on reuse. for dedicated, with a monthly commit, unit cost can be another ~30% lower once you amortize the cluster.
[02:05] Samir Patel: ok so if we have bursty traffic, does dedicated handle spiky opens? autoscaling?
[02:12] Miguel Torres: dedicated supports configured autoscaling and burst capacity options - you can set baseline dedicated nodes and allow burst to shared capacity. there's SLA bump for dedicated. but if your burst is extreme, cost for burst could be higher unless you provision for it.
[02:30] Evelyn Moore: can you map that to money? our $15k/month target - what size pilot can we run?
[02:37] Priya Rao: quick calcs - if your model averages 60 tokens per request and you expect 50k requests/day, that's ~3M tokens/day. naive hosted at list per-token would exceed 15k. but with KV caching on common prefixes (we saw reuse up to 40% for similar prompts) and batching during steady periods, you might reduce token billing to an effective 1.8M/day equivalent. that starts to look better. we need your exact prompt mix to run accurate sims.
[03:05] Laura Kim: we can share sample prompts. how do you measure caching effectiveness?
[03:10] Priya Rao: we provide an eval harness - you run your prompt set through our benchmark runner; it reports prefix reuse, batchability, latency SLOs, and estimated cost under hosted vs dedicated. Priya: we'll run this with you.
[03:22] Tom Briggs: what about data retention? logs, KV cache - where's the data stored?
[03:28] Alex Chen: hosted: we retain logs per your retention policy; you can request short retention or opt out; KV cache is encrypted, can be customer-controlled in Dedicated/Private. we'll include the data flow diagram in the pack.
[03:40] Samir Patel: performance - we need p95 < 350ms. what model variants? do you use quantized models to save cost?
[03:47] Priya Rao: yes, we support quantization-friendly execution and recommend model/quantization pairings per workload. often a 4-bit quantized variant gives big cost savings while keeping similar latency. Redwood runtime chooses kernels for best latency. For p95, we might pick a slightly larger variant on dedicated for predictability.
[04:07] Laura Kim: how do fallbacks work? if dedicated is saturated do you failover to hosted?
[04:13] Miguel Torres: yes - smart routing policies let you failover to compatible model variants or hosted pool to keep app online; you can configure cost vs latency prioritization.
[04:22] Evelyn Moore: finance question - what's the minimum commit for dedicated and typical discount curve?
[04:28] Alex Chen: minimum commit usually starts at mid-five figures monthly for GPU reserved pools; discounts scale with longer term and higher commit. For pilots, we often do a 3-month reserved with a smaller commitment + burst to hosted. we'll include sample pricing tiers.
[04:42] Samir Patel: any hidden costs - egress, storage, feature flags?
[04:46] Priya Rao: transparent billing - tokens and embeddings are primary, dedicated has baseline cluster fee, data egress billed at cloud provider rates if cross-region. optional add-ons: enhanced observability retention, SLA uplift. we'll lay all that out.
[05:00] Tom Briggs: security - can we get customer-managed KMS while on hosted? that was mentioned earlier.
[05:06] Alex Chen: hosted can integrate with customer KMS for certain pieces but for full control we recommend Dedicated/Private. we'll send KMS integration diagram and options.
[05:14] Laura Kim: pilot timeline - we want a 6 week pilot that proves cost per request and p95 latency. is that feasible?
[05:20] Miguel Torres: yes - typical pilot: week 1 onboarding + sample prompts, week 2-3 benchmark runs and tuning (batching/cache profiling), week 4-5 pilot on dedicated or hosted with real traffic, week 6 review and roll decision.
[05:33] Evelyn Moore: and contract terms after pilot? if dedicated needed, what commit length?
[05:37] Alex Chen: standard is monthly or annual reserved; we can offer a short-term pilot commit and apply credit toward longer term if you convert.
[05:45] Laura Kim: ok let's align next steps.
[05:47] Alex Chen: recap - we'll send pricing sheet + cost model, SOC2/KMS/security docs, and Priya will run the benchmark. Tom will share compliance constraints, Laura will share prompt set. any other blockers?
[05:59] Samir Patel: one small technical question - how does prefix KV cache work with streaming responses and long contexts?
[06:06] Priya Rao: KV cache stores repeated key/value states for shared prefixes so subsequent requests that reuse the prefix don't re-compute. with streaming we maintain incremental KV; long contexts need cache partitioning but it's supported - there are tradeoffs in memory usage vs hit rate. we'll share a short tech note.
[06:22] Laura Kim: perfect, thank you. talk soon.

End of call.
